name: FR-13 development thread set (step 7 phase 3)
status: DEVELOPMENT SET, NOT FROZEN. Drafted 8 November 2026 for step 7 phase 3 (D-93): the set the follow-up-focus changes are TUNED on, so it is never a test set and no result from it is reported as a measurement of FR-13. Drafted from the corpus files and the indexed chunks only; the frozen sets' files were not read, and the identifier-only overlap check (runs/2026-11-08/fr13-phase3-dev/) is the evidence of separation. Worded as users talk, with pronouns and ellipsis that need the earlier question.
corpus: The Objective 02 corpus, exactly as indexed from corpus/objective-02/manifest.json on kmp_obj02_20261101: 20 documents and 5 transcripts in 43 chunks. The scoped threads turn to D15 and D16, deliberately not the frozen set's D09 and T02.
notes: Two turns per thread: scripts/thread_set.py validates exactly two (D-86), so the brief's '2 to 3 turns' resolves to two.
Twelve threads: eight ordinary, two scoped asked by both roles, one topic change, one previous-answer follow-up (expected to fail with history, D-86 decision 2).
Thread ids start at t20 so no run id can be mistaken for the frozen set's t01-t09.
The previous-answer follow-up refers to a fact the first ANSWER introduces (inactivity), not the first question; under D-42 the reference should not resolve.
http_check entries exist because validation requires them; this set is run in-process only and the HTTP check stays on the frozen set.

scoring_rule.applies_to: Every run of every thread, all four ways, scored by the same rule as the frozen set.
parts: The rule is version 2 as implemented in scripts/thread_set.py, the same code path the frozen set is scored with: one outcome class per run; the expected-answer match is a listed phrase (substring, whitespace collapsed, case folded) or an accepted alternative (whole tokens), plus a cited listed source; a leak is an out-of-scope chunk, an out-of-scope partial match, or a restricted phrase in a role's verified statements. The canonical prose of the rule is frozen with corpus/objective-02/threads.json and is not restated here; this set exists to be scored by the same functions, not to redefine them.

turns.question: Do I need a doctor's certificate when I'm off sick?
And does time off looking after my kid come out of the same balance?
turns.spelled_out: Is carer's leave deducted from the same balance as personal leave?
turns.depends_on: 'the same balance' is the sick-leave balance the first turn is about; cold there is no balance to refer to.

turns.question: What do I have to attach when I claim back travel costs?
And when do I need sign-off before I pay for something?
turns.spelled_out: For a work expense, when do I need a department head's approval before spending the money?
turns.depends_on: 'sign-off before I pay' only reads as an expenses question through the first turn; cold it could as easily be procurement.

turns.question: What hours do I have to be contactable when I'm working from home?
expected_answer: ten in the morning to three in the afternoon

turns.question: How much notice does either side have to give to end it?
turns.spelled_out: How many weeks of written notice does it take for an employee or the manager to bring a working-from-home arrangement to an end?
turns.depends_on: 'it' is the remote arrangement from the first turn; cold there is nothing to end.

turns.question: Where do we write down that a customer agreed to us using their details?
What happens if they change their mind later?
turns.spelled_out: What happens when someone withdraws their consent to the use of their personal information?
turns.depends_on: 'they' are the consenting customers of the first turn, and 'change their mind' is withdrawing that consent.

turns.question: Which way do we go out from level three when the fire alarm goes off?
And who checks everyone has actually got out?
turns.spelled_out: Who confirms each area is clear during a fire evacuation?
turns.depends_on: 'got out' is the evacuation of the first turn; cold the question could be about leaving anything.

turns.question: What's the biggest risk the infrastructure team flagged at the standup?
Who's on call over that weekend?
turns.spelled_out: Who is on call on the Saturday and the Sunday of the Opal Junction cutover weekend?
turns.depends_on: 'that weekend' is the cutover weekend the first turn surfaced; cold no weekend is named.

turns.question: How many quotes do I need for a twenty thousand dollar purchase?
And at what point does it have to go out to tender instead?
turns.spelled_out: At what purchase value must a formal open tender be issued?
turns.depends_on: 'it' is the purchase from the first turn; cold there is no purchase on the table.

turns.question: Which room is the writing clear reports session held in?
And who's running it?
turns.spelled_out: Who facilitates the Writing clear reports training session?
turns.depends_on: 'it' is the session named in the first turn; cold there is no session at all.

turns.question: How do we handle a customer complaint the first person can't sort out on the spot?
And who on the team is strongest at that side of things?
turns.spelled_out: Who on the team holds the top rating for customer service in the skills matrix?
turns.depends_on: 'that side of things' is customer service, the subject of the first turn; cold there is no side of anything.

turns.question: When is the Melbourne office actually moving to the new building?
And how much has been put aside to pay for it?
turns.spelled_out: What is the budget for the office relocation project in the FY27 tracker?
turns.depends_on: 'it' is the office move from the first turn; cold there is nothing to pay for.

turns.question: How long do our passwords have to be these days?
What should I do if the room I reserved is occupied when I arrive?
turns.spelled_out: What should I do if the room I reserved is occupied when I arrive?

turns.question: Why had customers been cancelling before we could step in?
And how early do we now get in touch about that?
turns.spelled_out: At how many days of inactivity does the team now reach out to customers?
turns.depends_on: 'that' is the inactivity signal, which only the previous ANSWER introduces - the first question asks about cancellations. Under D-42 the reference should not resolve, which is what this thread measures.
